senses.gloss: m. (b. h.) sheet, usually of fine linen (cmp. σινδών; v. Sm. Ant. s. v. Pallium).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Yoma 3:4">Yoma III, 4</cite> <he>פרשו ס׳ של בוץ וכ׳</he> they spread a sheet of linen (for the high priest to walk on) between him &c.

<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Kilayim 9:3:3">Y. Kil. IX, 32ᵇ</cite> top <he>בס׳ אחד נקבר רבי</he> Rabbi was buried in one linen shroud (without any other garments); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Ketubot 12:3:3">Y. Keth. XII, 35ᵃ</cite> top.
<cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Yevamot 1:1:6">Y. Yeb. I, 2ᵇ</cite>; <cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 85:5">Gen. R. s. 85</cite> <he>דרך ס׳</he> each wrapped in a sheet (preventing direct contact).
<cite ref="Menachot 37b:8">Men. 37ᵇ</cite>, a. e. <he>ס׳ בציצית</he> a linen cloak with woollen show-fringes; a. fr.—Pl. <he>סְדִינִים</he>, <he>סְדִינִין</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Kelim 24:13">Kel. XXIV, 13</cite> <he>שלשה ס׳ הן</he> there are three classes of sheets with regard to Levitical purity.
<cite ref="Tosefta Keilim Metsia 1:14">Tosef. Kel. B. Mets. I, 14</cite> <he>ס׳ לצורות</he> canvas sheets for paintings; <he>ס׳ לאוהלים</he> sheets for awnings.
<cite ref="Tosefta Beitsah 2:13">Tosef. Bets. II, 13</cite> <he>ס׳ היו פרוסין</he> sheets (covering the floor of the dining room) were spread; Bab.
<cite ref="Beitzah 22b:11">ib. 22ᵇ</cite>; Y. ib. II, 61ᶜ bot.; a. fr.
